item.title: Thinking with Ecology: Lucia Pietroiusti and Olivia Whetung Online Conversation — Thu Oct 22, 12:00 PM
item.description:
The environment is often approached as an external issue to address. But what does it mean to focus on human relations with our more-than-human neighbours? This conversation engages with ecological thinking and how it is shaping artworks, institutional systems, and possible futures.
Curator, programmer, and strategist Lucia Pietroiusti stewards research and experimentation at the intersection of art, ecology, and systems. Pietroiusti is Head of Research & Emergence at the Hartwig Museum, Amsterdam. She was previously Head of Ecologies at Serpentine, London, and curator of the Golden Lion-winning opera-performance Sun & Sea, during the 58th Venice Biennale.
Artist Olivia Whetung is a member of Curve Lake First Nation. Whetung is from the area now called the Kawarthas and presently resides on Chemong Lake, Ontario. item.title: “Trade terror” and the right to development: Some reflections — Thu Oct 22, 12:30 PM — Faculty Common Room - 2027
item.description:

Abstract The Trump administration’s current approach to trade makes a break from the established rules of international trade and diplomacy. The approach may be described as “trade terror” because tariffs and trade restrictions are being employed – in an unpredictable manner – to coerce trading partners to accept trade deals/agreements or even force countries to agree to certain non-trade objectives.
In a globalised free market economy, free trade has been widely accepted as a key pathway to achieve economic growth, especially by developing countries. The 2025 Sevilla Commitment is a case in point. In this context, what does this new US approach to trade mean for the realisation of the right to development? item.title: Disaster Seminar Series: Community-Based Emergency First Response Teams: An Ontario Approach to Emergency Care and Disaster Preparedness in a Global Context — Thu Oct 22, 2:45 PM — 109 Atkinson Building (Harry Crowe Room) @ 4700 Keele Street
item.description: Join Y-EMERGE for our ongoing Disaster Seminar Series. This session will feature Jeffrey Gunner & Aaron Orkin, Director and Medical Director for the Emergency First Response Team (EFRT) program at Ornge, Ontario’s air ambulance service. Abstract: Emergency response begins with the people already there. In remote First Nations communities in northern Ontario, strengthening local capacity to respond to acute illness and injury addresses longstanding gaps in emergency care and offers a foundation for disaster preparedness. This seminar introduces the Emergency First Response Teams (EFRT) program: community-led, paid teams supported by Ornge through training, clinical oversight, equipment, and patient transport capabilities. item.description:

Pero antes de automatizar un proceso con IA, necesitamos entender cómo funciona y preguntarnos si realmente es la mejor forma de hacerlo.
En esta sesión práctica utilizaremos Microsoft Copilot como compañero para analizar y rediseñar un proceso.

If you are a beginner and or have health conditions this hike is not for you. 12km and it will be focused on high cardio. The trails are near Pickering, Ontario. item.title: 🍂🌿 NEW FALL WALK: Discover Biidaasige Park 🌿🍂 — Sun Oct 25, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! # 🍂🌿 **NEW FALL WALK: Discover Biidaasige Park** 🌿🍂
### A Brand-New Toronto Park, Fall Colours & Waterfront Trails
We're trying something **new**!
Join us for our first group walk to **Biidaasige Park**, one of the newest and most ambitious parks in Toronto. Opened as part of the massive transformation of the Port Lands, the park sits on **Ookwemin Minising**, Toronto's new island where the Don River meets Lake Ontario.
This isn't a walk we've done before, which makes it a little more exciting. We'll spend much of the afternoon actually **exploring the park rather than rushing through it** — following its trails, enjoying the waterfront, taking in the fall scenery, and stopping along the way to appreciate the new landscape. The park is enormous, with more than **50 acres already open** and more sections being added as the Port Lands transformation continues.

item.title: The InSECT Program, on Science Education, Citizenship, and Truth — Tue Oct 27, 10:00 AM
item.description: Harry Collins (Cardiff / UCL Institute of Education) A proposed new interdisciplinary teaching program in which science and engineering students learn alongside arts and humanities students, so that science teaching also becomes an education in democratic knowledge making instead of a purely technical exercise. Over the past half-century, historians, sociologists and philosophers have shown how scientific truth is constructed. From this many have concluded that science should be levelled down and brought into line with social values. We argue the opposite: science is an institution committed to correspondence truth about the observable world and to the moral duty of scientists to report their findings honestly. This makes science a model for democratic decision making and a bulwark against populists and autocrats, who are trying to erode truth in order to redefine ‘the will of the people’ however they please.
